micah: quick heads-up — on onboarding archon-3b (we converted from Llama vocab -> Mistral-style tokenizer) I'm seeing a weird cluster of vocab-boundary hits after conversion, plus a noticeable embed drift when we run int4 quant. low-hanging suspicion: token id remap / sentinel aliasing.

anya: can you paste the exact conversion command you ran? also what's the baseline metric you're seeing drift on (ppl / qa f1)?

micah: ran:```bash
python tools/convert_tokenizer.py --src-format=llama --dst-format=mistral --vocab-table=maps/llama2_to_mistral.json --out=archon_vocab.bin
```
smoke eval: fp16 ppl ~ 5.3, int4 ppl ~ 7.0, qa_f1 dropped 0.86 -> 0.71 on our squad-lite harness.

szymon: quick checklist: 1) off-by-one token id shifts (common) 2) reserved token collisions (<pad>/<eos>) 3) byte-level vs wordpiece normalization differences. simplest quick check: diff first 100 token ids and run a parity decode test. e.g.```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
A=Tokenizer.from_file('orig.json')
B=Tokenizer.from_file('converted.json')
for i in range(100):
    s=A.decode([i])
    t=B.decode([i])
    if s!=t: print(i, s, '->', t)
```

micah: pasted minimal diff — lots of low-frequency tokens (mostly accent/ligature-adjacent) were mapped to id 1 and 2 (reserved). sample: `token_id 4578: "▁Schröd" -> <|pad|>` and `token_id 4580: "é" -> <|unk|>`

katie: saw similar pattern when we converted gemma-lite earlier — downstream kv-cache misalignment shows up only in longcontext smoke: generation repeats after the remapped token appears in cache. could be our kv-indexing assuming contiguous vocab range.

micah: interesting — I ran the forward-compare for first 16 tokens with fp16 weights (no quant) and logits match within 1e-6. after int4 quant they diverge at step 3 when that remapped token is in input. so quant is amplifying the aliasing.

anya: can you run `tools/tokenizer-sanity --parity` and `tools/kv-alignment-check --seed 42 --len 1024` and paste outputs? also capture a short hex dump of token ids around the boundary.

micah: running now, will post short outputs.

eval-bot: smoke eval finished 
```
FP16: ppl=5.33, QA F1=0.86
INT4: ppl=7.02, QA F1=0.71
Token-alias-errors=0.0044 (per-token mismatch rate on test-set)
KV-mismatch-rate=0.12 (on 1024 windows)
Time: 00:12:34
```

szymon: plan suggestion: 1) tokenizer parity test to produce explicit mapping table (no silent remaps) 2) regenerate vocab with reserved tokens pushed to high ids if needed 3) run quantization bisect: int8->4bit symmetric->4bit per-channel to see where drift appears 4) rerun kv-index unit tests with remapped ids 5) add a smoke-case to CI that injects boundary tokens.

anya: agree. also add a quick patch to the converter that emits a `mapping_report.csv` listing src_id,dst_id,decoded_text and a flag for reserved collisions. will help audits.

micah: cool — I'll run tokenizer parity + mapping_report and drop the CSV here in ~20m. if anyone has a quick script to convert mapping -> tokenizer merge (that preserves contiguous top-k ids) share it pls.

katie: ping me when you have the mapping — I'll run longcontext kv-bisect and the generation smoke. :thumbsup:

micah: thanks — posting outputs soon.
